definition: Social comparison theory is a social psychology idea used to explain how comparing oneself with other people can influence thoughts, feelings, and behavior. In this packet, it is specifically applied to upward social comparison, where comparisons with people seen as doing better help explain how social pressure relates to turnover intention.
